Less than three years after graduating college in 1989, Jim Ziolkowski quit his corporate finance job at GE and started buildOn , an organization dedicated to building schools in impoverished nations and after school programs in America's inner city schools.
He was motivated by the poverty he witnessed during a year-long backpacking trip he took around the world after college, and by a celebration he came upon in Nepal.

|## James S. Hirsch - 2012
James Hirsch ('80) is a journalist and author who has written extensively about sports, race and social justice. His best-selling biography on Willie Mays, Willie Mays: The Life, the Legend , was named by The New York Times as one of the 100 notable books of 2010. The book culminated his love for baseball that began on the playgrounds of Clayton and has been nurtured by his many years following the Cardinals.
After graduating from Clayton High School in 1980, Hirsch earned his journalism degree at the University of Missouri and then his master’s degree from the LBJ School of Public Affairs at the University of Texas. He was a reporter for The New York Times for three years and The Wall Street Journal for nine years. He counts among his favorite stories essays on Barbara Jordan, Gregory Peck and his own grandmother.
In addition the biography of Mays, Hirsch has written the following nonfiction books: Hurricane: The Miraculous Journey of Rubin Carter, Riot and Remembrance: America’s Worst Race Riot and Its Legacy, Two Souls Indivisible: The Friendship That Saved Two POWs in Vietnam, Cheating Destiny: Living with Diabetes and A Reason To Believe , a collaboration with Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick. Hirsch is currently writing Walk in Their Shoes , a collaboration with global youth advocate Jim Ziolkowski.
* Hirsch lives in the Boston suburb of Needham with his wife Sheryl and their two children Amanda and Garrett.
